trends.label: Trends
trends.when: to describe how something is changing over time

phrases.t: There has been a marked rise in …

phrases.connector: …, which means that …, and as a result …

phrases.t: There has been a sharp decline in …
The figures show a clear upward trend in …

phrases.connector: …, and this pattern is likely to …

phrases.t: The long-term trend has been towards …

tasks.question: What are the most obvious changes you can see in the way people communicate?

models: There has been a marked rise in people messaging instead of calling, which suggests that voice calls are declining, and therefore texting has become the norm.
Video calls are steadily increasing, which means that distance matters less, and as a result people stay in touch more easily.

cues.cue: people / use / social media to talk
models: A growing number of people use social media to talk, and this shift reflects changing habits around messaging.
More and more, people rely on emojis to express emotion, and this development suggests written communication is becoming more casual.
Increasingly, conversations are moving online, and this pattern is likely to continue as technology advances.
The long-term trend has been towards instant messaging, and this is significant because it has reshaped how relationships are maintained.

tasks.question: How have people's shopping habits changed in recent years?

models: There has been a marked rise in people shopping online, which suggests that convenience now matters more than browsing in person, and therefore high street stores face pressure.
There has been a sharp decline in footfall in physical stores, largely because online shopping is more convenient, so many shops have closed.
A growing number of shoppers use mobile apps to buy things, and this shift reflects how central smartphones have become to daily life.
The figures show a clear upward trend in demand for same-day delivery, which indicates that customers expect speed as well as convenience.
Increasingly, consumers compare prices online before buying, and this pattern is likely to keep pushing retailers to offer better deals.
The long-term trend has been towards e-commerce, and this is significant because it is transforming the high street permanently.

tasks.question: What changes have you noticed in the way young people spend their time?

models: Increasingly, young people are moving to cities, and this pattern is likely to continue as job opportunities remain concentrated there.

cues.cue: young people / spend / time on screens
models: There has been a marked rise in the time young people spend on screens, which suggests that traditional hobbies are declining, and therefore outdoor activity is falling too.

cues.cue: young people / choose / to travel before university
models: A growing number of young people choose to travel before university, and this shift reflects a desire for independence.
More and more, young people pursue part-time jobs while studying, and this development suggests financial pressures are increasing.

cues.cue: young people's use of / streaming services / grow
models: Young people's use of streaming services is steadily increasing, which means that traditional television is losing its audience, and as a result broadcasters are adapting.

cues.cue: time spent / reading printed books / fall
models: The amount of time young people spend reading printed books has fallen dramatically, which highlights the fact that digital formats now dominate.

tasks.question: How has technology changed the way we study?

models: There has been a marked rise in students using online resources, which suggests that libraries are used differently now, and therefore study habits have changed.
A growing number of students take online courses, and this shift reflects greater flexibility in education.
The use of educational apps is steadily increasing, which means that learning happens outside the classroom too, and as a result students study more independently.

cues.cue: use of / AI tools for homework / rise
models: The figures show a clear upward trend in the use of AI tools for homework, which indicates that students are adapting quickly to new technology.
Increasingly, classrooms rely on digital devices, and this pattern is likely to grow as schools invest further in technology.
The long-term trend has been towards blended learning, and this is significant because it combines the best of online and in-person teaching.

tasks.question: What are the biggest changes you can see in your home town?

cues.cue: town / see / a rise in new housing
models: There has been a marked rise in new housing in my home town, which suggests that the population is growing, and therefore local services are under more pressure.
There has been a sharp decline in the number of small shops, largely because rents have increased, so many owners have had to close.
A growing number of cafes and restaurants have opened, and this shift reflects a growing interest in eating out.

cues.cue: traffic / rise / in the town centre
models: The figures show a clear upward trend in traffic in the town centre, which indicates that more people are commuting by car.
Increasingly, residents choose to cycle rather than drive, and this pattern is likely to continue as cycle lanes improve.

cues.cue: town / shift / towards a more modern feel
models: The long-term trend has been towards a more modern feel, and this is significant because it is changing the town's character.

tasks.question: How have people's eating habits changed over the years?

models: There has been a marked rise in people choosing plant-based diets, which suggests that health and environmental concerns are growing, and therefore demand for meat alternatives has increased.
There has been a sharp decline in the consumption of red meat, largely because people are more health-conscious, so alternatives have become popular.
A growing number of people read food labels carefully, and this shift reflects greater awareness of nutrition.
Demand for organic food is steadily increasing, which means that supermarkets stock more of it, and as a result prices are gradually falling.
More and more, people cook meals from scratch, and this development suggests a renewed interest in healthy eating.
Increasingly, families eat together less often, and this pattern is likely to continue as schedules become busier.
